content.text: Section 8 fully meets the preferred position, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Renewal terms sit at the preferred position: renewals are for successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year auto-renewal), Customer may opt out on only thirty days' written notice (well inside the ≤30-day preferred window), and Vendor must give a sixty-day renewal reminder, with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed. Clause 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of US CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent, matching the preferred CPI/3% cap, and adds ninety days' notice of any increase plus protection for prepaid periods. Section 7 contains no conflicting uplift mechanism (7.1 fixes Fees during the initial term). No redline needed.
